Exponential model for PFS and OS of Fleischer et al. (2009)

Source: R/ms_fleischer.R
ms_fleischer.Rd

Creates the ms_model in which the time to progression and the time to death are exponential and the hazard of death does not change at progression. Then OS is exponential with median median_os and PFS is exponential with median median_pfs.

Usage

ms_fleischer(median_pfs, median_os, dropout = 0)

Arguments

median_pfs

Median PFS.

median_os

Median OS (not smaller than median_pfs).

dropout

Dropout hazard.

Value

An object of class ms_model.

Details

With death hazard lambda_d = log(2) / median_os and PFS hazard log(2) / median_pfs, the progression hazard is log(2) / median_pfs - lambda_d. This is the model of Section 2 of Fleischer et al. (2009) with the hazard of death before and after progression equal to lambda_d.

References

Fleischer F, Gaschler-Markefski B, Bluhmki E (2009). A statistical model for the dependence between progression-free survival and overall survival. Statistics in Medicine 28:2669-2686.

See also

ms_model

Examples

m <- ms_fleischer(median_pfs = 6, median_os = 15)
ms_surv(m, time = c(6, 15), endpoint = "pfs")
#>   time      surv       haz       dens
#> 1    6 0.5000000 0.1155245 0.05776227
#> 2   15 0.1767767 0.1155245 0.02042204
ms_surv(m, time = c(6, 15), endpoint = "os")
#>   time      surv        haz       dens
#> 1    6 0.7578583 0.04620981 0.03502049
#> 2   15 0.5000000 0.04620981 0.02310491
